docs.text: 🎮 Create Your Own Catching Game! Welcome to the Scratch Catching Game course! In this guide, you will learn how to build your very own game where you control a character and catch falling objects. What you will create: A fun game where you move left and right to catch good items for points, avoid the bad items, and win the game! Before You Start What is Scratch? Scratch is a fun way to learn coding! Instead of typing hard words, you snap colorful blocks together like LEGO. It is the perfect place to create your own games, stories, and animations. What you need: A computer with internet access Your Scratch account (go to scratch.mit.edu to log in) A big imagination! 🧠✨ How to use this guide: Read each module step-by-step. Don't rush! Make sure to test your game often. If you see a challenge, try it out! 🛑 Listen to Teacher First! Wait! Before you begin: Your teacher is going to show you the basics on the screen. Please watch and listen carefully! Once the teacher says "Go!", you can come back to this guide and start making your game.

docs.text: 🎉 Congratulations! You did it! You have built a complete, working video game in Scratch. You learned how to use coordinates, loops, variables, and conditions. You are a real coder now! Next Challenges Do you want to keep going? Try adding these cool features to your game: - ⏱️ Timer Mode: Can you add a timer that counts down from 30 seconds? Try to get the highest score before time runs out! - 🛒 Shop Upgrade Mode: Use points to buy a faster character! - 👾 Boss Battle Mode: When you reach 20 points, a big boss appears! - 👯 Two Player Mode: Add a second player who uses the A and D keys to move. Who can catch the most? Keep creating and have fun! 🚀

docs.text: Module 4: Add Falling Objects What You Will Learn How to add an object to catch How to make it fall from the top of the screen How to make it reset when it hits the bottom Step-by-Step Instructions Add a new Sprite. This will be the object you want to catch! Add a when green flag clicked block (Events). Under it, add a forever loop (Control - orange). Inside the loop, put a change y by -5 block (Motion). This makes it fall! Now, drag an if <> then block (Control) inside the forever loop. Put a touching [edge]? block (Sensing - light blue) inside the if block. If touching the edge, make the object go back up using go to x: [pick random -200 to 200] y: 150 (Motion & Operators - green). Add Image Here [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the code blocks for the falling object, including the forever loop and the reset if touching the edge] Try It Yourself Click the Green Flag. Does your object fall down and then appear at the top again? Challenge Yourself Make the object fall faster by changing -5 to -10 . Checkpoint [ ] My object falls down continuously. [ ] My object teleports back to the top when it hits the bottom.

docs.text: Module 6: Add Score System What You Will Learn What a variable is How to create a Score How to add points when you catch an object Step-by-Step Instructions Go to the Variables category (dark orange). Click Make a Variable and name it Score . Go to your Backdrop's code (or Player code) and add: when green flag clicked -> set [Score] to 0 . Go back to your falling object's code. Find the if touching [Player] block. Inside that if , add change [Score] by 1 . Add Image Here [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the "Make a Variable" button and the blocks to set score to 0 and change score by 1] Try It Yourself Play the game and catch the object. Does your Score go up? When you click the Green Flag again, does the Score go back to zero? Challenge Yourself Give yourself 5 points for every catch instead of 1 point! Checkpoint [ ] My score goes up when I catch the object. [ ] My score resets to 0 when I restart the game.

docs.text: Module 7: Win Condition What You Will Learn How to set a score target How to show a "You Win" message Step-by-Step Instructions Go to your Backdrop's code. Add a new when green flag clicked block. Add a forever loop. Inside, add an if <> then block. For the condition, use the green Operator [ ] > [ ] . Put Score in the left box and 10 in the right box. If Score > 10, add a block to say [You Win!] for 2 seconds (Looks - purple), and then stop all (Control). Add Image Here [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the blocks that check if score > 10 and display the win message] Try It Yourself Play until you get more than 10 points. Does the game stop and tell you that you won? Challenge Yourself Instead of making the sprite say "You Win!", can you change the Backdrop to a special WIN screen? Checkpoint [ ] The game stops when I reach my score target. [ ] I see a "You Win!" message.

docs.text: Module 10: Add Sounds What You Will Learn How to find the Sound Library How to add sound effects for catching, losing points, and winning Step-by-Step Instructions Click on your player Sprite. Go to the Sounds tab at the top. Click the speaker icon to Choose a Sound (like "pop", "coin", or "magic spell"). Go back to the Code tab. When you catch a good object, use the start sound [pop] block (Sound - pink). Add a bad sound (like "bonk") when you touch an enemy! Add a happy sound when you win. Add Image Here [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the code with "start sound" blocks added for catching and hitting an enemy] Try It Yourself Play your game with the volume up! Challenge Yourself Can you add a background music track that loops forever? Checkpoint [ ] I hear a sound when I catch a good object. [ ] I hear a different sound when I hit an enemy.

docs.text: Module 12: Playtesting What You Will Learn How to test your game like a real game developer How to fix bugs Step-by-Step Instructions Swap seats with a partner. Let them play your game without you telling them how. Watch them play. Is it too hard? Too easy? Is anything broken? Write down one thing you can fix or improve. Go back to your computer and make that improvement! Add Image Here [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show a fun image of characters playing a game together or testing] Try It Yourself What did your partner think of the game? Did they find any bugs? Challenge Yourself Fix a bug your partner found before the showcase! Checkpoint [ ] I watched someone else play my game. [ ] I made at least one improvement based on testing.

docs.text: Module 8: Add Enemies What You Will Learn How to create objects you should avoid (like a bomb, ghost, or rock!) How to lose points Step-by-Step Instructions Add a new Sprite to be your enemy object. Copy the falling code from your good object to your bad object. (Hint: You can click and drag the code from one sprite to another!) In the enemy's code, change the catch detection: when touching [Player] , make it change [Score] by -1 (lose points!). Make sure the enemy also teleports back to the top after you touch it! Add Image Here [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the enemy code blocks where score is changed by -1] Try It Yourself Test your game. What happens to your score when you hit the enemy? Challenge Yourself Can you make the game end ("Game Over") if your score goes below zero? Checkpoint [ ] I have an enemy object falling. [ ] My score goes down when I touch the enemy.
